## **Clinical Trial**

#### Load the Gait data

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
load("data/gait.Rda")
```

1.  Plot each participants' gait data and describe it using descriptive statistics. Which of these descriptive statistics do you think is most useful for capturing the overall gait smoothness and balance of a participant?

    *Thoughts:*

    To plot each participants data, I first want to look at how the the data varies across the 700s. Therefore, I will create a histogram showing the counts for each angle observed across the timeframe

#### Check for Missing Values: 

```{r}
sum(is.na(gait_data))
```

No missing values, therefore continue with analysis. (Still need to check for outliers)

```{r}
#Obtain max and Min values
seconds <- gait_data[grepl("_secs$", names(gait_data))]

min(as.matrix(seconds), na.rm = TRUE)
max(as.matrix(seconds), na.rm = TRUE)
```

#### Histograms:

```{r}
#Histogram
#I want to take participant 1 (d004) and produce a datapoint for each time observation

# Change this ID to plot another participant
participant <- "d031"
values <- as.numeric(unlist(
  gait_data[gait_data$donorid == participant, measurement_cols]
))

hist(
  values,
  breaks = shared_breaks,
  xlim = c(-52, 62),
  xaxs = "i",
  xaxt = "n",
  main = paste("Gait measurements for", participant),
  xlab = "Measurement value",
  col = "steelblue",
  border = "white"
)

axis(1, at = c(-50, seq(-40, 50, by = 10), 60))
```

Now I want to apply this to each individual participant so then I can compare their histograms and gain insights into the distribution variations in gait_data

```{r}
measurement_cols <- grepl("_secs$", names(gait_data))
participants <- unique(na.omit(gait_data$donorid))

# Collect measurements for each participant
participant_values <- lapply(participants, function(id) {
  values <- as.numeric(unlist(
    gait_data[gait_data$donorid %in% id, measurement_cols]
  ))
  values[is.finite(values)]
})

# Calculate histograms and a shared y-axis limit
histograms <- lapply(participant_values, function(values) {
  hist(values, breaks = shared_breaks, plot = FALSE)
})

max_count <- max(vapply(histograms, function(h) max(h$counts), numeric(1)))

# Draw all histograms in a grid (4 × 4 for 16 participants)
local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  n_cols <- ceiling(sqrt(length(participants)))
  n_rows <- ceiling(length(participants) / n_cols)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(3, 3, 2, 1),
    mgp = c(1.8, 0.5, 0)
  )
  
  for (i in seq_along(participants)) {
    plot(
      histograms[[i]],
      freq = TRUE,
      xlim = c(-52, 62),
      ylim = c(0, max_count),
      xaxs = "i",
      xaxt = "n",
      main = as.character(participants[i]),
      xlab = "Measurement value",
      ylab = "Frequency",
      col = "steelblue",
      border = "white"
    )
    
    axis(1, at = seq(-50, 60, by = 10), cex.axis = 0.65)
  }
})
```

#### Interpretation of Multiple Histograms:

This works well to be able to see the frequency at which individuals are being recorded "off-axis". Histograms that are skinny and tall show little variation, and consistent alignment to 0º's, whilst spread out histograms represent participants with large variations from being 'straight', representing individuals with low stability/smoothness. This is visually good to compare, but may be hard to interpret as descriptive graphics.

#### Visual Representation of Vertical Axis Whilst Walking:

This graph will represent the vertical axis of each participant over their 700 second measurements. Organised into the two experimental groups (and exercise group).

```{r}
# Change participants ID numbers to 1-16
gait_data$participant_label <- paste("Participant", seq_len(nrow(gait_data)))

# Find measurement columns and put them in time order
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$", names(gait_data), value = TRUE
)

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[order(seconds)]

if (length(measurement_cols) == 0 || nrow(gait_data) == 0) {
  stop("No participant rows or seconds columns found.")
}

# Define the four groups using the labels in your dataset
treatment <- trimws(as.character(gait_data$treatment))
exercise <- tolower(trimws(as.character(gait_data$exercise)))

groups <- list(
  "Control\nNo Exercise" = which(
    treatment == "L-DOPA control" & exercise == "n"
  ),
  "Control\nExercise" = which(
    treatment == "L-DOPA control" & exercise == "y"
  ),
  "New Drug\nNo Exercise" = which(
    treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "n"
  ),
  "New Drug\nExercise" = which(
    treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "y"
  )
)

# Sort participants within each group by donor ID
groups <- lapply(groups, function(rows) {
  rows[order(gait_data$donorid[rows])]
})

# Check that everyone has been assigned to a group
if (sum(lengths(groups)) != nrow(gait_data)) {
  stop("Some treatment or exercise labels do not match the four groups.")
}

# Shared colour scale: blue at 0°, red at ±15° and beyond
angle_palette <- colorRampPalette(c("blue", "red"))(256)
red_threshold <- 20

local({
  old_par <- par(no.readonly = TRUE)
  on.exit(par(old_par))
  
  n_rows <- max(lengths(groups))
  n_cols <- length(groups)
  
  par(
    mfrow = c(n_rows, n_cols),
    mar = c(2.5, 1, 2, 1),
    oma = c(3, 0, 5, 0)
  )
  
  # Fill the grid row by row, keeping each group in its own column
  for (row in seq_len(n_rows)) {
    for (group in seq_along(groups)) {
      
      # Leave a blank panel if this group has fewer participants
      if (row > length(groups[[group]])) {
        plot.new()
        next
      }
      
      i <- groups[[group]][row]
      
      angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
        gait_data[i, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE]
      ))
      
      radians <- angles * pi / 180
      valid <- is.finite(radians)
      
      colour_index <- 1L + floor(
        pmin(abs(angles[valid]) / red_threshold, 1) * 255
      )
      
      angle_colours <- angle_palette[colour_index]
      
      # Create participant panel
      plot(
        NA,
        xlim = c(-1.1, 1.1),
        ylim = c(-0.01, 1.1),
        asp = 1,
        axes = FALSE,
        xlab = "",
        ylab = ""
      )
      
      # Semicircular guide
      arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)
      lines(sin(arc), cos(arc), col = "grey75")
      
      # Angle guides and labels
      ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)
      tick_radians <- ticks * pi / 180
      
      segments(
        0, 0,
        sin(tick_radians), cos(tick_radians),
        col = "grey80",
        lty = 2
      )
      
      text(
        1.12 * sin(tick_radians),
        1.12 * cos(tick_radians),
        labels = paste0(ticks, "°"),
        cex = 1
      )
      
      # Draw one ray per valid measurement
      segments(
        0, 0,
        sin(radians[valid]),
        cos(radians[valid]),
        col = adjustcolor(angle_colours, alpha.f = 0.5),
        lwd = 0.7
      )
      
      points(0, 0, pch = 16, cex = 0.6)
      mtext(
        gait_data$participant_label[i],
        side = 1,
        line = 0.5,
        cex = 0.8,
        font = 2
      )
    }
  }
  
  # Column headings
  for (group in seq_along(groups)) {
    mtext(
      names(groups)[group],
      outer = TRUE,
      side = 3,
      at = (group - 0.5) / n_cols,
      line = -1,
      font = 2,
      cex = 1.1
    )
  }
  
  mtext(
    "Walking orientation by participant",
    outer = TRUE, side = 3, line = 3.5,
    font = 2,
    cex = 1.4
  )
  
  mtext(
    "Distance from vertical: blue = 0° | red = 20° and above",
    outer = TRUE, side = 1, line = 1
  )
})
```

#### Visual Animation of Vertical Orientation:

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)

# Settings
participant <- "d031"
preview_seconds <- 30   # Use Inf for the full recording
red_threshold <- 20

# Find the participant
participant_row <- which(gait_data$donorid == participant)

if (length(participant_row) != 1) {
  stop("Expected exactly one row for participant: ", participant)
}

# Find measurement columns and order them by time
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$",
  names(gait_data),
  value = TRUE
)

if (length(measurement_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No measurement columns found.")
}

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
time_order <- order(seconds)

seconds <- seconds[time_order]
measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[time_order]

# Extract the participant's angles
angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
  gait_data[participant_row, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE],
  use.names = FALSE
))

# Select the preview period
keep <- seconds < min(seconds) + preview_seconds

animation_data <- data.frame(
  second = seconds[keep],
  angle = angles[keep]
)

if (nrow(animation_data) == 0) {
  stop("No measurements selected.")
}

# One frame per second requires consecutive second columns
if (any(diff(animation_data$second) != 1)) {
  stop("The selected measurement columns are not spaced one second apart.")
}

# Keep missing observations in the timeline, but show no orientation
animation_data$angle[
  !is.finite(animation_data$angle)
] <- NA_real_

# Convert angles to the endpoint of a line of length 1
animation_data$radians <- animation_data$angle * pi / 180
animation_data$x_end <- sin(animation_data$radians)
animation_data$y_end <- cos(animation_data$radians)
animation_data$deviation <- abs(animation_data$angle)

animation_data$angle_label <- ifelse(
  is.na(animation_data$angle),
  "Missing measurement",
  sprintf("Angle: %+.1f°", animation_data$angle)
)

# Explicitly preserve chronological frame order
animation_data$frame <- factor(
  animation_data$second,
  levels = animation_data$second
)

# Static semicircular guide
arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)

arc_data <- data.frame(
  x = sin(arc),
  y = cos(arc)
)

# Static angle guides
ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)

guide_data <- data.frame(
  x = sin(ticks * pi / 180),
  y = cos(ticks * pi / 180),
  label = paste0(ticks, "°")
)

# Build the animation
orientation_plot <- ggplot(animation_data) +
  geom_path(
    data = arc_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y),
    colour = "grey75"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = guide_data,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y),
    colour = "grey80",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = guide_data,
    aes(x = 1.12 * x, y = 1.12 * y, label = label),
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = 0,
      y = 0,
      xend = x_end,
      yend = y_end,
      colour = deviation
    ),
    linewidth = 3,
    lineend = "round",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(x = x_end, y = y_end, colour = deviation),
    size = 6,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  annotate(
    "point",
    x = 0,
    y = 0,
    size = 3,
    colour = "black"
  ) +
  # Position the angle readout closer to the animation
  geom_text(
    aes(label = angle_label),
    x = 0,
    y = -0.25,
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_colour_gradient(
    low = "blue",
    high = "red",
    limits = c(0, red_threshold),
    oob = scales::squish,
    breaks = c(0, 10, 20),
    labels = c("0°", "10°", "20°+"),
    name = "Distance from vertical"
  ) +
  # Reduce unused space below the pivot
  coord_fixed(
    xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25),
    ylim = c(-0.40, 1.25)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Walking orientation:", participant),
    subtitle = "Recording time: {current_frame} seconds",
    caption = "Negative angles shown left; positive angles shown right"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  transition_manual(frame)

# Render: one recorded second per animation second
orientation_animation <- animate(
  orientation_plot,
  nframes = nrow(animation_data),
  fps = 1,
  width = 650,
  height = 500,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)

# Save and display in the rendered Quarto HTML
animation_file <- paste0("orientation_", participant, ".gif")

anim_save(
  filename = animation_file,
  animation = orientation_animation
)

knitr::include_graphics(animation_file)
```

#### Stick Figure Animation:

Representing this as a stick figure animation will help with conceptualisation of walking gait when presenting information

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(gganimate)

# Settings
participant <- "d031"
preview_seconds <- 30   # Use Inf for the full recording
playback_fps <- 10      # Use 1 for real-time playback
red_threshold <- 20

# Find the participant
participant_row <- which(gait_data$donorid == participant)

if (length(participant_row) != 1) {
  stop("Expected exactly one row for participant: ", participant)
}

# Find measurement columns and put them in time order
measurement_cols <- grep(
  "^[0-9]+_secs$",
  names(gait_data),
  value = TRUE
)

if (length(measurement_cols) == 0) {
  stop("No measurement columns found.")
}

seconds <- as.numeric(sub("_secs$", "", measurement_cols))
time_order <- order(seconds)

seconds <- seconds[time_order]
measurement_cols <- measurement_cols[time_order]

# Extract the participant's angles
angles <- as.numeric(unlist(
  gait_data[participant_row, measurement_cols, drop = FALSE],
  use.names = FALSE
))

# Select the preview period
keep <- seconds < min(seconds) + preview_seconds

animation_data <- data.frame(
  second = seconds[keep],
  angle = angles[keep]
)

if (nrow(animation_data) == 0) {
  stop("No measurements selected.")
}

if (any(diff(animation_data$second) != 1)) {
  stop("The selected measurement columns are not spaced one second apart.")
}

# Preserve missing observations in the timeline
animation_data$angle[
  !is.finite(animation_data$angle)
] <- NA_real_

# Prepare angles and frame labels
animation_data$radians <- animation_data$angle * pi / 180
animation_data$deviation <- abs(animation_data$angle)

animation_data$angle_label <- ifelse(
  is.na(animation_data$angle),
  "Missing measurement",
  sprintf("Angle: %+.1f°", animation_data$angle)
)

animation_data$frame <- factor(
  animation_data$second,
  levels = animation_data$second
)

# Semicircular guide
arc <- seq(-pi / 2, pi / 2, length.out = 200)

arc_data <- data.frame(
  x = sin(arc),
  y = cos(arc)
)

# Angle guides
ticks <- seq(-90, 90, by = 45)

guide_data <- data.frame(
  x = sin(ticks * pi / 180),
  y = cos(ticks * pi / 180),
  label = paste0(ticks, "°")
)

# Upright stick figure, pivoting midway between the feet
body_template <- data.frame(
  part = c("torso", "left_arm", "right_arm", "left_leg", "right_leg"),
  x    = c(0,    0,     0,    0,     0),
  y    = c(0.38, 0.70,  0.70, 0.38,  0.38),
  xend = c(0,   -0.24,  0.24, -0.13, 0.13),
  yend = c(0.82, 0.48,  0.48, 0,     0)
)

# Repeat body segments for every frame
body_data <- merge(
  animation_data,
  body_template,
  by = NULL,
  sort = FALSE
)

# Rotate the body: positive angles lean right
body_data <- transform(
  body_data,
  rotated_x    = x * cos(radians) + y * sin(radians),
  rotated_y    = -x * sin(radians) + y * cos(radians),
  rotated_xend = xend * cos(radians) + yend * sin(radians),
  rotated_yend = -xend * sin(radians) + yend * cos(radians)
)

# Rotate the head's centre
animation_data$head_x <- 0.90 * sin(animation_data$radians)
animation_data$head_y <- 0.90 * cos(animation_data$radians)

# Build the animation
orientation_plot <- ggplot() +
  geom_path(
    data = arc_data,
    aes(x = x, y = y),
    colour = "grey75"
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = guide_data,
    aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = x, yend = y),
    colour = "grey80",
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = guide_data,
    aes(x = 1.12 * x, y = 1.12 * y, label = label),
    size = 4
  ) +
  # Torso, arms and legs
  geom_segment(
    data = body_data,
    aes(
      x = rotated_x,
      y = rotated_y,
      xend = rotated_xend,
      yend = rotated_yend,
      colour = deviation
    ),
    linewidth = 2.5,
    lineend = "round",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  # Head
  geom_point(
    data = animation_data,
    aes(x = head_x, y = head_y, colour = deviation),
    shape = 21,
    fill = "white",
    size = 12,
    stroke = 1.8,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  # Angle readout positioned close to the figure
  geom_text(
    data = animation_data,
    aes(label = angle_label),
    x = 0,
    y = -0.25,
    size = 5
  ) +
  scale_colour_gradient(
    low = "blue",
    high = "red",
    limits = c(0, red_threshold),
    oob = scales::squish,
    breaks = c(0, 10, 20),
    labels = c("0°", "10°", "20°+"),
    name = "Distance from vertical"
  ) +
  # Compact plotting area
  coord_fixed(
    xlim = c(-1.25, 1.25),
    ylim = c(-0.40, 1.25)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = paste("Walking orientation:", participant),
    subtitle = "Recording time: {current_frame} seconds",
    caption = "Schematic figure tilted by the recorded angle"
  ) +
  theme_void(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  ) +
  transition_manual(frame)

# Render
orientation_animation <- animate(
  orientation_plot,
  nframes = nrow(animation_data),
  fps = 1,
  width = 650,
  height = 500,
  renderer = gifski_renderer()
)

# Save and display in Quarto HTML
animation_file <- paste0("stick_figure_", participant, ".gif")

anim_save(
  filename = animation_file,
  animation = orientation_animation
)

knitr::include_graphics(animation_file)
```

#### Descriptive Statistics for Gait Data:

Getting Interquartile range, max, min, mean (Boxplots).

Grouped by Treatment Group, ordered by IQR size

```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Convert the time columns into one measurement column
gait_long <- gait_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^[0-9]+_secs$"),
    names_to = "time",
    values_to = "gait_value"
  )

# Order participants by ascending IQR
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(treatment, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(treatment, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label)

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Create one boxplot per participant
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = treatment
)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    outlier.colour = "red",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(treatment),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of gait measurements by participant",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Individual boxplots for Control and Treatment group:

```{r}
# Convert the time columns into one measurement column
gait_long <- gait_data |>
```

Now making groups by age bracket (turning binary) and producing boxplots:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Calculate the median age across participants
median_age <- gait_long |>
  distinct(participant_label, age) |>
  summarise(cutoff = median(age, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  pull(cutoff)

median_age  # View the cutoff

# Create two age groups
gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    age_group = case_when(
      age < median_age  ~ "Younger",
      age >= median_age ~ "Older"
    )
  )

# One boxplot per age group
ggplot(
  filter(gait_long, !is.na(age_group)),
  aes(x = age_group, y = gait_value, fill = age_group)
) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = c("Younger", "Older")) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements by age group",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Median age: ", round(median_age, 2),
      " years; younger < median, older ≥ median"
    ),
    x = NULL,
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Separate into the four experimental groups:

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Define the four groups
gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    group = case_when(
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "n" ~
        "control + no exercise",
      grepl("control", treatment, ignore.case = TRUE) & exercise == "y" ~
        "control + exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "n" ~
        "treatment + no exercise",
      treatment == "New compound" & exercise == "y" ~
        "treatment + exercise"
    ),
    group = factor(
      group,
      levels = c(
        "control + no exercise",
        "control + exercise",
        "treatment + no exercise",
        "treatment + exercise"
      )
    )
  )

# Order participants by IQR within each group
participant_order <- gait_long |>
  group_by(group, participant_label) |>
  summarise(iqr = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(group, iqr) |>
  pull(participant_label) |>
  as.character()

gait_long <- gait_long |>
  mutate(
    participant_label = factor(
      participant_label,
      levels = unique(participant_order)
    )
  )

# Plot the four groups
ggplot(gait_long, aes(
  x = participant_label,
  y = gait_value,
  fill = group
)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.colour = "red", na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(-60, 60, by = 15)) +
  coord_flip(ylim = c(-60, 60)) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(group),
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait measurements by treatment and exercise",
    x = "Participant",
    y = "Gait measurement"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

Assumptions to Check:

If I want to run a linear or mixed linear model;

- A normal linear regression assumes independence of outcome data. This is not true, as the 700 observations are in a time series to each participant.

```{r}

```

Other tests worth analysing:

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# One row per participant
participant_stats <- gait_long |>
  group_by(donorid, treatment, exercise, age) |>
  summarise(
    n_observations = sum(!is.na(gait_value)),
    mean_gait = mean(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_gait = median(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_gait = sd(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_gait = IQR(gait_value, na.rm = TRUE),
    rms_gait = sqrt(mean(gait_value^2, na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    treatment = factor(treatment),
    exercise = factor(exercise, levels = c("n", "y"))
  )

participant_stats
```

Using Root Square Mean to compare deviations from upright:

```{r}
model_treatment <- lm(
  rms_gait ~ treatment,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_treatment)
confint(model_treatment)
```

Using Standard Deviation:

```{r}
model_treatment <- lm(
  sd_gait ~ treatment,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_treatment)
confint(model_treatment)
```

Checking the reference group:

```{r}
levels(participant_stats$treatment)
```

Accounting for exercise and age, Using RMS:

```{r}
model_adjusted <- lm(
  rms_gait ~ treatment + exercise + age,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_adjusted)
confint(model_adjusted)

# Test each predictor while accounting for the other two
drop1(model_adjusted, test = "F")
```

Accounting for Exercise and Age, using SD:

```{r}
model_adjusted <- lm(
  sd_gait ~ treatment + exercise + age,
  data = participant_stats
)

summary(model_adjusted)
confint(model_adjusted)

# Test each predictor while accounting for the other two
drop1(model_adjusted, test = "F")
```

Running graph for Root Square Means:

```{r}
ggplot(
  participant_stats,
  aes(x = treatment, y = rms_gait)
) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.5,
    fill = "grey90",
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = exercise, size = age),
    position = position_jitter(width = 0.08, height = 0, seed = 345),
    alpha = 0.7
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("n" = "#D55E00", "y" = "#0072B2"),
    labels = c("n" = "No exercise", "y" = "Exercise"),
    name = "Exercise"
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(
    name = "Age (years)",
    range = c(1, 6),
    guide = guide_legend(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, NA),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.1))
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Gait deviation from upright by treatment",
    x = "Treatment",
    y = "Participant RMS (degrees)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
